newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to change T-bill terms at Wednesday auction.
newsitem.headline: Russia to change T-bill terms at Wednesday auction.

text.p: The terms of Russian government securities to be auctioned on Wednesday will be changed from those announced last week, but details will only be issued later on Tuesday, the Central Bank said.
A central bank official gave no explanation for the move.

But uncertainty about a new tax on government securities forced the authorities last week also to cancel an auction of new GKO discount Treasury bills and instead auction a new tranche of older paper.
Only new issues are subject to the tax, whereas new tranches of existing issues do not come under it.

The Finance Ministry had been planning to issue 7.00 trillion roubles of 273-day paper, which would have come under the new tax, and a new 4.00 trillion rouble 504-day tranche of an OFZ interest-bearing government bond.

The new tax, which technically came into force this month, imposes the usual profits tax, which is 43 percent for banks and 35 percent for other entities, on government securities, while setting a 15 percent rate on interest from bond coupons.
Government officials had intended the new tax to be levied at a rate of 15 percent on all earnings from government securities, including gains on discount paper.
The Finance Ministry and Federal Tax Service have written to the Justice Ministry saying the tax should be interpreted in this way, but the Justice Ministry has not yet approved this letter.
